QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_34

question.text: A Section 8 Company under the Companies Act 2013 is defined by which of the following key features?

answer.text: Its objective is promotion of commerce, art, science, research, education, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any such other object; it applies its profits in promoting its objectives; and it prohibits payment of any dividend to its members.
It must have minimum 100 members and paid-up capital of Rs 5 crore.
It must be a wholly-owned subsidiary of a listed company.
It pays dividends only out of reserves, not current profits.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Box 2.2, the Companies Act defines a Section 8 company as one whose objective is promotion of commerce, art, science, research, education, social welfare, religion, charity, protection of environment or any such other object; applies its profits in promoting objectives; and prohibits payment of any dividend to members. Section 8 companies can organise on a share basis but shares are not residual claims on profits. **The Trap:** Option B invents capital/member thresholds. Option C invents a subsidiary-only restriction. Option D muddles with conventional company dividend rules. **Cross-Exam Context:** XII (Securities Markets Foundation), XV (RA) treat Companies Act basics. V-B (MF Foundation) treats corporate legal forms. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When your client is a Section 8 company, annex a copy of the SRN-filed Section 8 licence from MCA to your engagement file — the licence number is a standard cross-check during SEBI inspection of SSE-listed Section 8 entities.
